sections.html:
Westminster is a home rule city roughly 9 miles north-northwest of downtown Denver. In the 2020 census it had 116,317 residents: 71,240 on the Adams County side and 45,077 on the Jefferson County side. Its borders touch Broomfield, Thornton, Northglenn, Federal Heights and Arvada.

Check the county first. It decides which treasurer sends your tax bill, which clerk records your deed and which assessor sets your value. The top of your tax bill names the county that sent it.

sections.h2: Older housing and what it means for a sale
sections.html:
The city stayed small until the 1950s and then expanded fast. It had 1,686 people in 1950, 13,850 in 1960, 50,211 in 1980 and 100,940 in 2000. Most of its housing therefore dates from the postwar decades, and Westminster's own rental code states that it exists to address the deterioration of aging rental housing.

For an owner, the result is a wide spread of house ages. Buyers look closely at roofs, furnaces and plumbing in the older stock, and a seller who knows those answers has an easier conversation.

Every residential rental in Westminster has to hold either a license or a registration under the city's Rental Code, which matters if you own a rented house and want to sell it. The rules separate larger rental properties from smaller ones.

  • Four or more units, or four or more rental dwellings under one owner in a townhome or condo community, call for a license.
  • License fees are $50 per rental property. Inspections cost $40 per unit, or $20 per income-restricted unit.
  • Single-family houses, duplexes and up to three townhomes or condos under one owner need registration only, with no fee and no required inspection.
  • Systematic inspections apply to rentals six years old or older with four or more units.
  • Single-family and duplex rentals are inspected after a complaint, or sooner if the owner asks.

When you sell a house with a tenant in it, confirm that the registration is current. The city's rental property line is 303-706-3026, and the program is described on the City of Westminster Rental Property Inspections page.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates in Adams and Jefferson counties
sections.html:
The two counties follow the same state calendar. A first-half payment is due by the end of February, a second half by June 15, or the whole bill by April 30. Each year's bill covers the previous year, since both counties collect in arrears.

Payment or noticeAdams CountyJefferson County
Tax noticesSent in JanuaryMailed by the end of January
First halfFebruary 28February 28, or the next business day if the office is closed that day
Full paymentApril 30April 30
Second halfJune 15June 15
Delinquent noticesMailed in JulyMailed in July
Tax lien saleOnline, each fallOnline, held in November

The Jefferson County Treasurer is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden, open Monday to Thursday and closed Fridays. Adams County posts its dates on the Adams County due dates page, and Jefferson County keeps its calendar on the Important Dates page.

sections.h2: Getting around: US 36, the B Line and the park-n-ride
sections.html:
Interstate 25, US 36, US 287 and State Highways 95, 121 and 128 all cross the city. US 36 runs toward both Denver and Boulder. RTD's Flatiron Flyer buses use the express lanes there, and the Westminster Center Park-n-Ride sees about 1,546 weekday boardings and about 498 buses per day.

The B Line opened in 2016 and carries commuters about 6 miles from Westminster Station to Denver Union Station. A house a short drive from the station or the park-n-ride gives a commuting buyer an easy pitch, and you can use that when you describe your home.

sections.h2: Open space and the Downtown Westminster project
sections.html:
Voters first approved a sales tax for open space in 1985, and the city now owns more than 3,000 acres, including large areas at Standley Lake Regional Park and the Westminster Hills area. The Big Dry Creek Trail covers about 12 miles, and the US 36 Bikeway links into a trail system of more than 145 miles.

Downtown Westminster is a 105-acre redevelopment on the old Westminster Mall site, demolished in 2012. It has an Alamo Drafthouse and a 125-room hotel, with plans for about 2,300 multifamily, condo and townhouse units. Homes near trails and the new downtown tend to draw more questions from buyers.

Standley Lake and the creek trails also bring a practical matter. A buyer may ask whether a lot sits near a waterway, so know your answer before the first showing.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works for a Westminster homeowner
sections.html:
A buyer who pays cash does not wait on a bank, so the closing does not depend on loan approval. You get an offer, decide whether it works, and set a closing date with the title company.

That arrangement suits a tenant-occupied house, an inherited property or a home that needs work, because no repair list stands between you and the sale. Westminster owners usually contact us after a job transfer, an inheritance or a long stretch with the house empty. If the house is a rental, settle the registration first so the title company has no surprises.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
Start by telling us the address, the county it is in, and whether anyone lives there. We reply with a written cash offer. If you accept, the title company confirms ownership, finds any lender payoff and checks the tax bill with the right treasurer. You then choose the closing date. For a rental, give the title company the registration or license paperwork and the lease so a tenant's rights are clear before closing.

Bring identification and the latest tax bill. If the bill is from Jefferson County and you need to visit the Treasurer in person, plan around the Monday to Thursday hours.

After closing, the deed is recorded in the county where the house sits, and your tax and utility accounts are moved to the new owner. Keep a copy of the settlement statement for your records.

Two small checks save time. First, make sure the mailing address on file with the county is current, so a late notice is not lost while the house changes hands. Second, ask the title company to show how the tax bill is split between you and the buyer. Both counties bill a year behind, so the split matters more than most sellers expect.

faqs.q: Is Westminster in Adams County or Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Both. Westminster lies in western Adams County and northeastern Jefferson County. In the 2020 census, 71,240 residents were on the Adams side and 45,077 on the Jefferson side.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Westminster?
faqs.a: The rental must hold a current license or registration while you own it. Single-family houses, duplexes and up to three condos or townhomes under one owner are registered at no fee. Properties with four or more units need a license at $50 per property, plus $40 per unit for inspection.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Westminster?
faqs.a: The first half is due by the end of February, the full amount by April 30, and the second half by June 15. Check whether your bill came from Adams or Jefferson County.
The RTD B Line, which opened in 2016, runs about 6 miles from Westminster Station to Denver Union Station.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westminster house with repair needs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as is, so you do not need to fix the roof, flooring or fixtures before closing.
